excerpt: Converting video and audio has never been so easy. $ ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.avi
A complete, cross-platform solution to record, convert and stream audio and video.
ffmpeg reads from an arbitrary number of inputs (which can be regular files, pipes, network streams, grabbing devices, etc.)
Set the video bitrate of the output file to 64 kbit/s: ffmpeg -i input.avi -b:v 64k -bufsize 64k output.mp4
Force the frame rate of the output file to 24 fps: ffmpeg -i input.avi -r 24 output.mp4

Streamcopy is useful for changing the elementary stream count, container format, or modifying container-level metadata. Since there is no decoding or encoding, it is very fast and there is no quality loss.
Selecting which streams from which inputs will go into which output is either done automatically or with the -map option
A simple video filtergraph that performs deinterlacing (using the yadif deinterlacer) followed by resizing (using the scale filter)
Frames from second input are overlaid over those from the first. Frames from the third input are rescaled, then the duplicated into two identical streams.
ffplay is a minimalistic multimedia player.
ffprobe is a simple analysis tool to inspect multimedia content.
libavfilter provides means to alter decoded audio and video through a directed graph of connected filters.
libavdevice provides an abstraction to access capture and playback devices.
libavformat implements streaming protocols, container formats and basic I/O access.
Coding examples are available in the doc/examples directory.
Doxygen documentation for current trunk (regenerated nightly); documentation for the 9.0, 8.1, 8.0...
Decoders use the same hwaccel API and commands, so users do not need to do anything special to enable them
Support for Vulkan encoding, with H264 and HEVC was merged. This finally allows fully Vulkan-based decode-filter-encode pipelines
all the major components of the transcoding pipeline (demuxers, decoders, filters, encodes, muxers) now run in parallel.
The libavformat library can now read and write IAMF (Immersive Audio) files. The ffmpeg CLI tool can configure IAMF structure with the new -stream_group option.
the VVC decoder, merged as experimental in version 7.0, has had enough time to mature and be optimized enough to be declared as stable.
MV-HEVC decoding is now supported. This is a stereoscopic coding tool that begun to be shipped and generated by recent phones and VR headsets.
Cropping metadata is now supported with Matroska and MP4 formats.
Vulkan compute-based codecs: ProRes encoding and decoding, DPX decoding
replaced by the AVChannelLayout API allowing such features as custom channel ordering, or Ambisonics.

Critic of the funding stance: the reported issue is a reproducible use-after-free in a codec that ships by default with most desktop and server distributions. They worry it could be exploited against legacy devices and say they would not fund people who dismiss such reports as slop.

Commenter siding with FFmpeg: Google used AI to find a use-after-free that would have taken seconds to fix. Generating bug reports that burden volunteers instead of submitting fixes 'leaves a very sour taste.'

User says they use FFmpeg and Whisper to record and transcribe live police scanner audio for their city, updating a live website in real time. 'It works great, with the expected transcription errors and hallucinations.'
Skeptic thinks adding Whisper to FFmpeg is bloat, 'especially when the feature doesn't work flawless, whisper is very limited.'

'Impressed anytime I have to use it,' even though they must restudy the man page, ask an LLM, or use a GUI to build the right incantation. Calls it an indispensable transcoding multitool and thinks building processing on Vulkan 1.3 was the right move.

'ffmpeg is a treasure.' It cuts through proprietary and arcane codec/format roadblocks and never hits a commercial paywall. However, 'the CLI is of course quite opaque and the documentation for various features is often terse.'
User extracted frames of a 1993 anime film in 15-minute segments with FFmpeg and upscaled them with Real-ESRGAN-ncnn-vulkan. They then recombined the frames into a 4K upscale.
Workflow complaint: about half the effort goes into assembling long complex CLI commands and half into fighting shell escaping. Adding text to video brings its own escaping hell.
'Pretty insane software. I use it all the time.' Their only wish is animated webp support.

User welcomes the new compute-shader (Vulkan) encoders/decoders for cross-platform acceleration of codecs beyond H.264/H.265/AV1. They say the new ProRes encoder already looks useful for their project.

Biggest struggle with FFmpeg was finding clear documentation and examples for the API (libav), not the CLI. Tutorials are either CLI-only or outdated, so they have to read FFplay's source to catch up on the workflow each time.
User built a GUI that calls ffmpeg to cut clips by start time and duration. Depending on the start point, the output has a noticeable stretch of black video.

On a project with Apple .mov files, ffmpeg lost color information (gamma, contrast, chroma). Apple Compressor preserves it via ICC profiles derived from QuickTime headers, so they had to stop using ffmpeg for that project.

User chops large videos with FFmpeg and loves how fast it is. Not being an expert, they wrote a batch file wrapper for in/out points and file paths, plus a help screen with examples for when they forget the params.

On Windows with Nvidia, h264_nvenc gives about an 8x boost, and the user wonders why ffmpeg doesn't auto-detect it. They also saw better speed without h264_videotoolbox on macOS Sequoia. At work they once avoided buying GPU cloud servers after noticing the installed ffmpeg was compiled without GPU acceleration.
User says ffmpeg lately drives their webcam more reliably than Google Chrome, despite its unusual, bespoke command syntax.

'ffmpeg has always felt like a gui application crammed into tui format.' Having used the C API a few times, they say it is straightforward in many respects but 'makes invalid states extremely easy to represent.'
Comparison: one user stopped using ffmpeg entirely and uses only GStreamer for intense video work. They find GStreamer's pipeline-based command line and docs more sensible.

Workaround for inscrutable syntax: using '-/filter_complex file_name' to load a filtergraph from a separate, nicely formatted file finally let them 'crack' ffmpeg. They built motion detection inside a single ffmpeg process.

Several users say they use ffmpeg so infrequently that the syntax never sticks, so they now rely on LLMs to generate commands. One recalls losing whole days in the past trying to make it do a specific set of things.
